why.text: Steep Danube terraces of weathered rock and loess, where Atlantic and Pannonian climates meet and big day-night swings keep the whites acidic.

styles.text: Mostly white wines; red wines are a very small share.

climate.text: Atlantic and Pannonian climates meet: above-average rain, hot days and cool nights. The Danube tempers heat and harsh winters, and cool Waldviertel winds widen day-night swings before harvest.

soil.text: Weathered bedrock on the terraces, with loess layers on the eastern sides of the rock slopes. Medieval stone terraces make the steep slopes workable.

tastes.text: Whites: greenish yellow, apple, pear and citrus, with high acidity; older Grüner Veltliner shows pepper and apricot. Reds: fruity and low in tannin, with sour cherry and redcurrant.

styles.name: Gebietswein
styles.text: Wachau DAC without a village or vineyard name; 17 listed grapes, blends allowed.

styles.name: Ortswein
styles.text: Wachau DAC naming a village; nine listed grapes, hardly any oak tone allowed.

styles.name: Riedenwein
styles.text: Single-vineyard Wachau DAC from Grüner Veltliner or Riesling; no chaptalisation, hardly any oak.
